problem_statement: shadcn/next-contentlayer is a Next.js App Router blog powered by Contentlayer MDX, reframed as Tidewatch — a coastal field journal of tides, wrack lines, and estuary weather. Its shared chrome is a top navigation bar rendered from a shared nav registry (app/config/nav-links.ts, each item an anchor carrying the nav-link class) mounted in the root layout (app/layout.tsx via components/site-nav.tsx) above the main content, closed by a shared footer (components/site-footer.tsx); the journal exposes a shared card pattern for grouped content — a local image, an h3 headline, and a short note paragraph (components/field-card.tsx). The team has built a curated Fieldbook page at the /fieldbook/ route that gathers the foundational entries a shore walker should start from, composed from the shared card pattern. Because the Fieldbook now lists six subjects (tides, the wrack line, estuary weather, the salt marsh, and shore-log/first-walk-kit basics), the page needs its OWN topic filter so a reader can narrow the entries by coastal subject instead of scanning all six. BUILD that topic filter as a native part of the Fieldbook page: a row of topic tab controls (All entries, Tides, Wrack line, Estuary, Salt marsh, Log & kit) above the shared FieldCard grid, plus a live readout that reports the active subject and how many entries match, in the form “Showing N of 6 · <Category>”. Clicking a topic tab must FILTER the shared card grid to that subject AND update the live readout to match (clicking Log & kit shows the two log/kit cards and the readout reads “Showing 2 of 6 · Log & kit”); the readout must never go stale relative to the shown cards. Keep the Fieldbook entry REGISTERED in the shared nav registry (app/config/nav-links.ts) so a nav-link for Fieldbook renders cross-page on both the Home page and the Fieldbook page. The tab row must wrap and remain readable and tappable at desktop, 834px tablet, and 390px mobile with no horizontal overflow, and the active tab and readout must stay legible (no overlapping or clipped tabs, no dark-on-dark or invisible active state). Preserve the home post feed, the About page, the post detail routes, and the shared top-nav and footer.
required_content: The Fieldbook page at /fieldbook/ presents at least six curated entries composed from the shared card pattern (local image + h3 headline + note paragraph) and does not render the not-found page.

The Fieldbook page hosts a topic filter above the card grid: a row of topic tab controls (All entries, Tides, Wrack line, Estuary, Salt marsh, Log & kit) plus a live readout in the form “Showing N of 6 · <Category>”.

Clicking a topic tab filters the shared card grid to that subject AND updates the live readout to match; clicking Log & kit shows the two log/kit entries and the readout reads “Showing 2 of 6 · Log & kit”.
The live readout stays consistent with the shown cards after every tab click — it never remains frozen at the initial “Showing 6 of 6 · All entries” once a subject has been selected.

A Fieldbook entry is registered in the shared nav registry (app/config/nav-links.ts) so a nav-link anchor for Fieldbook renders through the shared top-nav on both the Home page and the Fieldbook page.
The Fieldbook page is wrapped in the same shared chrome as the rest of the journal (shared top navigation bar and shared footer).

Desktop, 834px tablet, and 390px mobile layouts of both Home and Fieldbook have no horizontal overflow; the topic tab row wraps and stays readable and tappable, and the active tab and readout remain legible.
design_constraints: Compose the Fieldbook grid from the existing shared card pattern (image + h3 + note paragraph); do not invent a divergent bespoke row/list layout for it.
Build the topic filter as a native control of the Fieldbook page that operates on the page's own card grid; do not bolt on an unrelated widget or metric strip.
Register the Fieldbook link in the shared nav registry so it renders cross-page through the same shared top-nav on Home and Fieldbook; do not ship the page in isolation without the shared navigation.
The filter's live readout must be recomputed from the active topic on every click so it never disagrees with the visible cards.
Use existing local images and shared assets from the repo (public/blog-post-*.jpg); avoid external stock images or generated mockups.
Keep the implementation inside the current Next.js App Router / Tailwind structure; do not introduce a new framework or CMS.

The topic tab row must wrap intentionally on small viewports (no fixed single-line row that overflows) and the active tab and readout must stay legible (adequate contrast, no overlapping or clipped tabs).
state_constraints: desktop_initial, tablet_initial and mobile_initial capture the Tidewatch home with its shared top-nav (nav-link anchors, including the Fieldbook nav-link in the reference) and post feed.

desktop_fieldbook_component, mobile_fieldbook_component and tablet_fieldbook capture the Fieldbook page: the shared card grid (>=6 entry cards each with an image, an h3 headline, and a note paragraph) with the topic filter row and the live readout, reachable through the shared Fieldbook nav-link.

desktop_fieldbook_filter is captured AFTER clicking the Log & kit topic tab: the grid shows the two log/kit cards and the readout reads “Showing 2 of 6 · Log & kit”; desktop_fieldbook_estuary and desktop_fieldbook_all_reset capture other tab selections and the reset to All entries.
mobile_fieldbook_filter captures the same Log & kit selection at 390px; the tab row must wrap without horizontal overflow.
desktop_about and desktop_home_feed capture the preserved About page and home post feed with the shared chrome intact.

change_completion: The Fieldbook page renders at /fieldbook/ (not the not-found page) with >=6 shared cards (image + h3 + note).
The topic filter row and the live “Showing N of 6 · <Category>” readout render above the shared card grid.
Clicking the Log & kit tab filters the grid to the two log/kit cards and updates the readout to “Showing 2 of 6 · Log & kit”.
design_consistency: The grid is composed from the shared FieldCard pattern (image + h3 headline + note paragraph), not a bespoke off-system layout.
The Fieldbook nav-link is registered in the shared nav registry and renders cross-page through the shared top-nav on Home and Fieldbook.
The topic filter is a native control of the Fieldbook page operating on the page's own card grid, styled to match the journal.
regression: The home post feed, the About page, and the post detail routes still render with the shared top-nav and footer intact.
No shared chrome (nav registry / site-nav / site-footer) is broken by the change.
responsive: Desktop, 834px tablet, and 390px mobile layouts of Home and Fieldbook have no horizontal overflow.
The topic tab row wraps on small viewports and the active tab and readout stay legible and tappable (no overlapping/clipped tabs, no dark-on-dark active state).

author_notes: Product-grade L4 Consistency (design_continuity) task on a Next.js App Router + Contentlayer MDX blog reframed as the Tidewatch coastal field journal. The native lever is the curated Fieldbook page's OWN topic filter over the shared FieldCard grid (image + h3 headline + note paragraph, from components/field-card.tsx), with a live “Showing N of 6 · <Category>” readout — the editorial-blog genre's natural way to let a reader narrow curated entries by subject. Four orthogonal gates: D6 mobile overflow on the tab row (reference wraps, defect pins a fixed 640px single line); D2 cross-page presence of the shared Fieldbook nav-link (class nav-link) on Home and Fieldbook via the shared nav registry; D3 visual_regression on the filter panel (the broken solution shingles/clips the tabs and renders the active tab dark-on-dark illegible); D4 interaction_assertions on the live readout after clicking Log & kit (the broken solution snapshots the readout in a useState initializer so it stays frozen at “Showing 6 of 6 · All entries” while the grid re-filters). Uses the repo's own local images public/blog-post-*.jpg and Tailwind; no new framework, no external assets, no bespoke off-system layout.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: Next.js App Router blog powered by Contentlayer MDX (shadcn/next-contentlayer) reframed as the Tidewatch coastal field journal, whose shared chrome ships a design system — a shared nav registry rendering nav-link anchors, a shared card pattern (image + h3 + note), and a shared footer. A design_continuity Consistency task to ADD a new Fieldbook page that conforms to that shared card pattern and registers its link in the shared cross-page navigation without diverging into an off-system one-off.
